# Dimension 5: Sync & Interoperability

Reference file for the Todoist PA integration research.
See [citations.md](../citations.md) for source details.

## Google Calendar 2-Way Sync

### Todoist → Google Calendar

| Change in Todoist | Effect in Google Calendar |
|-------------------|--------------------------|
| Time-blocked task created | Event appears on "Todoist" calendar [5] |
| Task name changed | Event name updated [5] |
| Date/time/duration changed | Event time updated [5] |
| Task completed | Checkmark added to event name; event remains [5] |
| Task deleted | Synced event removed [5] |
| All-day task | Syncs only if "Sync all-day tasks" toggle enabled [5] |

### Google Calendar → Todoist

| Change in Google Calendar | Effect in Todoist |
|---------------------------|-------------------|
| Event name changed | Task name updated [5] |
| Event start date changed | Task date updated [5] |
| New event created | NO task created [5] |
| Single recurring instance edited | Does NOT sync back [5] |
| Complex recurrence patterns | Does NOT sync [5] |

### Limitations

- Tasks from shared projects don't sync unless assigned to the user [5]
- Complex recurrence patterns unsupported: "every other", "every X days" in Google Calendar;
  "hourly recurrence", "multiple weekdays in same month" in Outlook [5]
- Completing a recurring task in Todoist does NOT update Google Calendar to avoid
  duplicate events [8]

## Slack Integration

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| Create tasks | `/todoist` slash command with due dates, labels, project names [6] |
| Message-to-task | Three-dot menu → "Add a task" [6] |
| Complete tasks | From Slack via "More options" dropdown [6] |
| Change assignee | From Slack [6] |

### Limitations

- Single workspace only — no multi-workspace support [6]
- Tasks in private projects or Inbox can't be assigned to others [6]
- Individual account setup required (not team-wide) [6]
- Available on Free, Pro, and Business plans [6]

## Duplicate Signal Management

### The Problem

When Todoist syncs to Google Calendar, the PA sees the same task in two places:
1. **Todoist API** — the canonical task with full metadata
2. **Google Calendar API** — a synced mirror event on the "Todoist" calendar

### Recommended Strategy

1. **Designate Todoist as authoritative for personal tasks.** When the PA reads Google
   Calendar, filter out events from the "Todoist" calendar [5].
2. **Detection heuristic**: Todoist-synced events appear on a dedicated "Todoist" calendar
   that the integration creates [5]. The PA should check the calendar name/ID.
3. **Slack has no read-side duplication**: Todoist's Slack integration only creates tasks
   (write-side), so the PA won't see duplicate data from Slack [6].
4. **Single sync path rule**: Never use both Todoist's built-in calendar sync AND a
   third-party tool (Reclaim, Zapier calendar sync) simultaneously [5][40].

## Recurring Task Behavior

When a recurring task is completed [8]:
- Task resets with next occurrence date (does not disappear)
- Completed instance logged in Activity log
- Does NOT move to completed tasks list
- PA will see the task "reappear" with a new due date

Completed instances retrievable via `GET /api/v1/tasks/completed_by_completion_date` [1].

## Real-Time Update Options

### Webhooks

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Events | item:added, item:updated, item:deleted [3][27] |
| Delivery | HTTPS POST [27] |
| Verification | HMAC-SHA256 [27] |
| Requirements | HTTPS endpoint, no custom ports, OAuth app [27] |

Webhooks require a publicly accessible HTTPS endpoint, which adds infrastructure
complexity for a local-first PA.

### Sync API Polling

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Endpoint | POST /api/v1/sync [2] |
| Mechanism | sync_token for incremental updates [2] |
| Rate limit | 50 requests/min [2] |
| Latency | Depends on polling interval |

For a local-first advisory PA, Sync API polling is simpler than webhooks:
- Every 5 minutes: 12 req/hour, negligible rate limit usage
- Every 1 minute: 60 req/hour, well within 50/min limit (just barely)
- Every 10 minutes: 6 req/hour, minimal API usage

Recommended: **5-10 minute polling interval** via Sync API for a personal PA.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 Local Machine                     │
│                                                  │
│  ┌─────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Claude API  │◄──►│ MCP Clients (stdio)    │  │
│  │  / Agent SDK │    │ ┌── Todoist MCP [14]   │  │
│  └──────┬──────┘    │ ├── Jira MCP           │  │
│         │           │ ├── GitHub MCP          │  │
│         │           │ ├── Google WS MCP       │  │
│         │           │ └── Slack MCP           │  │
│         │           └────────┬───────────────┘  │
│         │                    │                  │
└─────────┼────────────────────┼──────────────────┘
          │                    │
    ┌─────▼─────┐    ┌────────▼────────┐
    │ Claude API │    │ Platform APIs    │
    │ (Anthropic)│    │ ┌─── Todoist    │
    │            │    │ ├─── Jira       │
    │            │    │ ├─── GitHub     │
    │            │    │ ├─── Google     │
    │            │    │ └─── Slack      │
    └────────────┘    └─────────────────┘
```

Todoist adds a 6th data source to the existing PA architecture. For deduplication,
the PA filters Google Calendar's "Todoist" calendar events.

## Gaps and Limitations

- Webhook event catalog may be broader than documented (project, note events?) [3]
- Whether webhooks can be filtered to specific projects/labels is unknown [27]
- Recommended Sync API polling interval not officially documented [2]
- Google Calendar → Todoist sync is partial (no new event → task creation) [5]
